mainTopic: The unwritten איסור of a daughter from an אנוסה, הן והן גופי תורה, and the new פרק's limits on teaching עריות, מעשה בראשית and the מרכבה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the first פרק. A man's daughter from a woman he raped is forbidden even though the Torah never says so outright. רבא learns the איסור from a גזירה שוה on הנה and learns the punishment from a גזירה שוה on זימה. The גמרא then corrects the משנה's wording to הן והן גופי תורה: every topic, written outright or not, is an essential part of the Torah. After the הדרן, the second פרק opens with a משנה limiting how hidden topics are taught. עריות may not be taught to three, מעשה בראשית not to two, and the מרכבה not even to one unless he is a wise student who understands on his own. The משנה also warns against prying into what is above, below, before and after the world. The גמרא rereads the מרכבה clause as 'to one student', with an exception for a wise student. Two attempts to find the עריות rule hinted in a פסוק fail, so רב אשי limits it to סתרי עריות and grounds it in logic: with three students, two may miss the teacher and permit something forbidden, since the desire for עריות is especially strong. Finally, a ברייתא learns from the singular word 'שאל' that מעשה בראשית is taught to one student only, and sets limits on what may be asked.

steps.title: The ערוה that is not written: his daughter from a woman he raped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the example of an ערוה that is not stated outright in the Torah: a man's daughter born from a woman he raped.
steps.simpleTranslation: This refers to his daughter from the woman he raped, which is not written explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering which part of עריות is not written in the Torah. The answer is a man's daughter from a woman he raped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists many forbidden relatives, but it never says outright that a man may not be with his own daughter. She is still forbidden, so the איסור must come from a hint in the פסוקים. The case is a daughter from an אנוסה because she is not his wife's daughter, so the איסור of 'a woman and her daughter' does not cover her.

keyTerms.meaning: the woman he raped (not his wife)
to his daughter
which is not written (explicitly in the Torah)
forbidden relationships

steps.confusionAlert: The daughter from his wife is already forbidden as 'a woman and her daughter.' The new point is only about a daughter whose mother he never married.

phrases.english: To his daughter from the woman he raped,
phrases.notes: This line finishes an answer that began just before: what in עריות is not written outright?

phrases.english: which is not written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question (asked before this section) of what in עריות is not explicit.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A man's daughter from his אנוסה is forbidden, but this is not written explicitly in the Torah.

steps.title: The איסור is learned from הנה and הנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רבי יצחק בר אבדימי, shows that the איסור is derived through a גזירה שוה on the word הנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי told me that it is derived from 'הנה' and 'הנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the unwritten איסור actually comes from. It is learned by linking two פסוקים that both use the unusual word הנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק uses הנה about 'a woman and her daughter,' and another uses הנה about a son's or daughter's daughter. The shared word links the two, so any daughter of a woman he was with, even an אנוסה, is forbidden to him. This is why the משנה can say עריות 'have something to rely on.'

keyTerms.meaning: it comes / it is derived
'they', an unusual form used in the פסוקים of עריות
linking two פסוקים through a shared word

phrases.english: As Rava said,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi said to me:
It is derived from 'hena' and 'hena.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17 and ויקרא 18:10.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא, אֲמַר לִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי: אָתְיָא ״הֵנָּה״ ״הֵנָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the unwritten איסור named in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a daughter from an אנוסה is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word הנה, linking ויקרא 18:17 with ויקרא 18:10.

steps.title: The punishment is learned from זימה and זימה
steps.stepSummary: A second גזירה שוה, on the word זימה, is used for this איסור as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is derived from 'זימה' and 'זימה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second link between פסוקים, this time through the word זימה. This brings in the punishment for this ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first link (הנה) only shows that the act is forbidden. The word זימה appears both in the איסור of 'a woman and her daughter' and in the פסוק that gives the punishment of burning. Linking them carries the punishment over to this case too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'lewdness', a word found in several פסוקים of עריות
death by burning

phrases.english: It is derived from 'zima' and 'zima.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17 and ויקרא 20:14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second גזירה שוה after the one in step 2, this time for the punishment.
steps.raayaObject: The punishment for being with a daughter from an אנוסה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word זימה, linking ויקרא 18:17 with ויקרא 20:14.
steps.whatToRemember: A daughter from an אנוסה is not written in the Torah. Her איסור comes from the הנה–הנה link, and her punishment from the זימה–זימה link.

steps.title: Are only these topics essential, and not the others?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase הן הן גופי תורה and objects that it seems to exclude the other topics from being essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'These are the essential parts of the Torah.' Are these essential, and those not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and challenges how it is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הן הן, 'these are the ones,' sounds like it singles out only the topics just listed as essential. That would wrongly suggest the other topics in the משנה, like שבת and חגיגה, are not essential parts of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: the essential parts of the Torah
'These yes, those no?', a formula for objecting to what a phrase leaves out

phrases.english: These are the essential parts of the Torah.
These, yes, and those, no?
phrases.notes: 'These' are the topics just named in the משנה; 'those' are the other topics listed before them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts discussing a new line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording הן הן גופי תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording seems to exclude the other topics from being essential, which cannot be correct.

steps.title: Read it as: both these and those are essential
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the reading to הן והן גופי תורה: both groups are essential parts of the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'These and those are the essential parts of the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by changing how the משנה should be read: from הן הן to הן והן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the letter ו turns 'these are the ones' into 'these and those.' Now the משנה teaches that every topic it mentioned is essential, whether it is written outright or rests on hints.

keyTerms.meaning: 'rather, say', which introduces a corrected reading
these and those, meaning both groups

phrases.english: Rather, say:
These and those are the essential parts of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: הֵן וְהֵן גּוּפֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the reading of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the topics just listed are essential.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the topics in the משנה are essential parts of the Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: The correct reading is הן והן גופי תורה: every part of the Torah is essential, whether written outright or not.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of הכל חייבין
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of מסכת חגיגה, called הכל חייבין, is formally closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'All are obligated.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the first פרק of חגיגה with the traditional closing line. No new argument is made here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a farewell to the chapter, expressing that we will come back to learn it again. It marks the end of the discussion about who must come to the בית המקדש and what was learned about גופי תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing formula said at the end of a פרק
'All are obligated': the name of the first פרק of חגיגה, taken from its opening words

steps.whatToRemember: The first פרק, הכל חייבין, is now complete. A new topic begins in the next step.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'All are obligated'
phrases.notes: A פרק is named by its first words. This one opened with 'הכל חייבין בראייה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose final discussion ended with הן והן גופי תורה in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of חגיגה is concluded.

steps.title: Limits on who may hear deep topics taught
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that עריות may not be taught to three, מעשה בראשית not to two, and מרכבה not even to one, unless he is a wise student who understands on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not teach the laws of forbidden relations to three students, nor the story of Creation to two, nor the מרכבה to even one, unless he is wise and understands on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The second פרק opens with a משנה that sets a maximum number of students for three sensitive topics. The more hidden the topic, the smaller the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a clear ladder: עריות may be taught to up to two, מעשה בראשית to only one, and מרכבה not even to one. The last line, 'unless he is a חכם who understands on his own', opens an exception for a special kind of student.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not expound or teach in depth
Forbidden relationships
The workings of Creation
The Divine Chariot (the vision in יחזקאל), a deep hidden topic
Understands on his own, from his own mind

steps.confusionAlert: 'Three' and 'two' are the forbidden numbers, not the allowed ones. עריות may be taught to two, but not to three.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the basis for the tradition of guarding hidden Torah topics and teaching them only to fitting students.

phrases.english: One may not expound forbidden relations before three,
nor the act of Creation before two,
nor the Chariot by oneself,
unless he is wise
and understands on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עריות may not be taught to three, מעשה בראשית not to two, and מרכבה not to one, unless the student is a חכם who understands on his own.

steps.title: Warning against prying into four hidden matters
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: whoever probes what is above, below, before, and after would have been better off never being born, and the same goes for one who ignores his Maker's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever looks into four things would have been better off not coming into the world: what is above, what is below, what was before, and what will be after. And whoever does not care about the honor of his Maker would have been better off not coming into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues in the same spirit and gives a strong warning against searching into matters beyond human reach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After limiting how these topics are taught, the משנה now limits what a person may investigate at all: the four 'directions' beyond the created world. It closes by explaining the root problem: prying where one is not allowed shows a lack of respect for כבוד קונו.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gazes or looks deeply into
It would be better (a mercy) for him
The honor of his Maker

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה teaches two things: limits on how hidden topics are taught (step 7), and limits on what one may probe at all (this step).

phrases.english: Whoever looks into four matters,

phrases.aramaic: רָתוּי לוֹ כְּאִילּוּ לֹא בָּא לָעוֹלָם:
phrases.english: it would be better for him as if he had not come into the world:
what is above, what is below,
what is before, and what is after.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁלֹּא חָס עַל כְּבוֹד קוֹנוֹ,
phrases.english: And anyone who has no concern for the honor of his Maker,
it would be better for him not to have come into the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from teaching limits to limits on personal investigation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not probe what is above, below, before, or after, and one must care for the honor of his Maker.

steps.title: The מרכבה line seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the משנה first says the מרכבה may not be taught even to one person, and then says it may be taught to a wise student who understands on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said at first: not the מרכבה even before one. Then you said: unless he is wise and understands on his own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the new משנה by pointing out that the line about the מרכבה seems to say two opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביחיד, 'by oneself', sounds like a person may not study the מרכבה at all, even alone. But the very next words allow it for someone who is wise and understands on his own. The גמרא wants to know how both parts fit together, and the next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: You said in the first part
And then you said
A single individual

phrases.english: GEMARA: You said in the first clause:
nor the Chariot by oneself,
and then you said:
unless he is wise
and understands on his own!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרַתְּ בְּרֵישָׁא וְלֹא בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה בְּיָחִיד וַהֲדַר אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first גמרא discussion on the new משנה, aimed at the מרכבה clause from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause: ולא במרכבה ביחיד אלא אם כן היה חכם ומבין מדעתו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביחיד ('by oneself') sounds like no one may study the מרכבה at all, even alone. The second half then allows it for a wise person, so the two halves seem to clash.

steps.title: How to Read the משנה: One Student Only If He Is Wise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction by reading the משנה as one connected rule. The מרכבה may not be taught even to one student, unless he is a חכם who understands on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: One may not teach עריות to three students, nor מעשה בראשית to two, nor the מרכבה even to one, unless that one is wise and understands on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9 by showing how the משנה should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question came from reading ביחיד as 'by oneself', as if even studying alone were banned. The גמרא rereads it as ליחיד, 'to one student'. The rule is about a teacher teaching one student, and the exception is that the student may be taught if he is wise and understands on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. A formula for explaining the intended reading of a text
Teach in depth, expound
To a single person
Understands on his own, from his own mind

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
One may not expound forbidden relations to three,
nor the act of Creation to two,
nor the Chariot to one,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה חָכָם וּמֵבִין מִדַּעְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: unless he was wise and understands on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: ביחיד is read as ליחיד (teaching to one student), and the second clause sets the exception for that student
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ביחיד means 'by oneself', so the משנה bans even studying the מרכבה alone and then contradicts itself by allowing a wise person
steps.terutzMaskana: The מרכבה may not be taught even to one, except to a wise student who understands on his own
steps.whatToRemember: The מרכבה is taught to no one, except a single חכם who already understands on his own.

steps.title: Why Not Teach Forbidden Relations to Three?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about עריות and asks for its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one may not expound עריות before three. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by asking for the source of the first rule in the משנה. This sets up the suggested answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave numbers: three for עריות, two for מעשה בראשית. The גמרא now wants to know where the number three comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Forbidden relationships

phrases.english: One may not expound forbidden relations before three.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new line, asking for the source of the first rule in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for not expounding עריות before three

steps.title: A Suggested Source: The Double Word ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the number comes from the פסוק ״אִישׁ אִישׁ אֶל כׇּל שְׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ״. The two words ״אִישׁ״ count as two, ״שְׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ״ adds one, and the Torah says not to come close to that group.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because it is written: "Man, man, to any of his close relatives." "Man, man" is two, "his close relative" is one, and the Torah says, "Do not come close to uncover nakedness."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible source for the number three, starting with "if you say," which hints it may be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double word ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ is read as two people, and ״שְׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ״ as a third. Together they make three. The warning that follows is then read as "do not approach these laws with a group of three."

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. Introduces a suggestion that may be rejected
His close relative
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or השם

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written:
"Man, man, to any close relative of his."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:6

phrases.english: "Man, man" is two,
"his close relative" is one,
and the Merciful One says: "Do not come close to uncover nakedness."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק. Here it is read as a warning not to study these laws as three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proposed answer to the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count of ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ (two) plus ״שְׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ״ (one) gives three

steps.title: Challenge: The Same Double Word Appears Elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ also appears by cursing השם and by מולך. Would we then say those topics may not be taught to two?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, it is written: "Man, man, who curses his God," and "Man, man, who gives of his children to the Molech." Would you say the same there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggested source by pointing to other פסוקים with the same double word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ always means a count of two people for teaching, then the laws of cursing השם and of מולך should also have a limit on how many may learn them. No such limit exists, so the method seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, from now on. Introduces an absurd result of the last idea
An idol worshipped by passing children through fire
So too? Would it be the same?

phrases.english: But if so, that which is written:
"Man, man, who curses his God,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:15

phrases.english: "Man, man, who gives of his children to the Molech,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:2

phrases.english: would it be so too?
phrases.notes: He means: would those laws also be forbidden to teach to two people? That makes no sense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source proposed in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ as a count of students
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same double word in other פסוקים would create teaching limits that do not exist

steps.title: Those Double Words Include Gentiles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in those other פסוקים, ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ is needed for something else. It teaches that גוים are also warned against cursing השם and against עבודה זרה, just like Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, those cases are needed to include גוים, who are warned about cursing השם and about עבודה זרה just like Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the suggested source. The double word in the other פסוקים is already used for a different teaching, so it cannot teach a count of students there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A double word can only teach one extra idea. By cursing השם and by מולך, ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ is used up to include גוים. By עריות it is free to teach the count of three, so the challenge is answered for now.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for something else
To include
Are warned, are forbidden
Literally "blessing השם." A polite way of saying cursing השם

phrases.english: Rather, those are needed by him
to include the gentiles,
who are warned about "blessing" God
phrases.notes: "Blessing" here is a polite way of saying cursing. The גמרא avoids writing the harsh word.

phrases.english: and about idol worship, like Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 and defends the source from step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: The other verses' double word is already used for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ should teach a count of students
steps.terutzMaskana: By cursing השם and מולך, ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ includes גוים, so it does not teach a count there
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not end the discussion. In the next step the גמרא turns this same answer against the ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ source for עריות.

steps.title: The עריות verse is also needed to include gentiles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ by עריות is also needed to teach that גוים are warned about עריות. So it cannot be the source for the rule of three.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ by עריות is also needed to include the גוים, who are warned about עריות just like Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from step 14 against the original source. The ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ by עריות is also busy teaching something else, so it cannot be the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, the גמרא said ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ by cursing השם and by מולך is used to include גוים. The same is true here: ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ by עריות includes גוים in the עריות prohibitions. So the counting method from step 12 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
To include
Warned / commanded not to do

phrases.english: This one too is needed
phrases.notes: "This one" means the ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״ in the עריות פסוק from step 12.

phrases.english: to include the gentiles
who are warned about forbidden relations, like Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of step 14's answer to knock out the source from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from ״אִישׁ אִישׁ אֶל כׇּל שְׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ״ in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word already used for one teaching (including גוים) cannot also be used to count people for the rule of three.

steps.title: A new source: ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת מִשְׁמַרְתִּי״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different פסוק. ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם״ counts as two, ״מִשְׁמַרְתִּי״ counts as one, and the פסוק then warns not to do the abominable customs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is the פסוק ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת מִשְׁמַרְתִּי״. ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם״ means two, ״מִשְׁמַרְתִּי״ means one, and the Torah says ״לְבִלְתִּי עֲשׂוֹת מֵחֻקּוֹת הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old source and offers a new פסוק from the end of the עריות section. It is a new answer to the question in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The counting method is the same, but the פסוק is different. The plural word ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם״ stands for two people and ״מִשְׁמַרְתִּי״ adds a third. The warning in the same פסוק is read as telling us to guard against a group of three.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall keep My charge
Two
One
Abominations

phrases.english: Rather, from what is written:
"And you shall keep My charge,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:30

phrases.english: "And you shall keep" counts as two,
phrases.notes: The word is plural ("you all"), so it is read as at least two people.

phrases.english: "My charge" counts as one,
and the Merciful One said:
"Not to do any of the abominable customs."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 rejects the first source, this step offers a replacement source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for not teaching עריות before three (from step 11).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count of words in ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת מִשְׁמַרְתִּי״ (2+1=3), together with the warning that follows it.

steps.title: ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם״ also appears by שבת, מצות, and קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new source. ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם״ is also written about שבת, מצות, and קדשים. Would those topics also be forbidden to teach before three?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, it is also written ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת״, ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת״, and ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֵת מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ״. Would the same rule apply there too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the source from step 16 by showing the same word in other places. Nobody says those topics are limited to fewer than three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם״ hinted at a limit of three, the limit should apply wherever the word appears. But שבת, מצות, and קדשים are taught openly to everyone. So the word alone cannot be the source.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if that is so (opens a challenge from the logic just given)
So too? (Would it really be the same here?)
The charge of the holy things

phrases.english: But if so, what about what is written:
"And you shall keep the Shabbat,"
phrases.notes: שמות 31:14

phrases.english: "And you shall keep the matzos,"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:17

phrases.english: "And you shall keep the charge of the holy things,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:5

phrases.english: would it be so there too?
phrases.notes: He means: would we also say those topics may not be taught before three? Clearly not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new source from step 16, the same way step 13 challenged step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears by other מצוות that have no such teaching limit, so the word cannot create the limit.

steps.title: רב אשי: the rule is only about the hidden details of עריות
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the משנה differently. ״אֵין דּוֹרְשִׁין בָּעֲרָיוֹת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה״ means one may not expound סתרי עריות, the hidden details of עריות, before three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: what does ״אֵין דּוֹרְשִׁין בָּעֲרָיוֹת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה״ mean? It means one may not expound the hidden parts of עריות before three.
steps.whatsHappening: After both פסוק sources fail, רב אשי takes a new approach. He redefines what the משנה's rule covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not about all of עריות. It covers only סתרי עריות, the details that are not spelled out openly in the פסוקים. With this narrower reading, the גמרא no longer looks for a word-count hint in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Expound, explain in depth
The hidden details of forbidden relations

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of not teaching עריות before three applies only to סתרי עריות, the hidden details, not to the topic as a whole. Two attempts to find it hinted in a פסוק were rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי is saying עריות cannot be taught at all to three. Only the hidden details are limited.

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said:
What does "one may not expound forbidden relations before three" mean?
One may not expound the hidden parts of forbidden relations before three.
phrases.notes: "Hidden parts" means the details not written openly in the פסוקים, which are learned by drawing them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 knocks out the second source, רב אשי sets aside the search for a word-count source and redefines the scope of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the משנה's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covers all of עריות and needs a counting hint in a פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only סתרי עריות, the hidden details, which may not be expounded before three.

steps.title: The reason for the limit of three is logic
steps.stepSummary: The rule against teaching סתרי עריות to three comes from logic. With three students, two may talk to each other, miss the teacher's words, and come to permit something forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is logic. When two students sit before their teacher, one discusses with the teacher and the other listens closely. With three, one discusses with the teacher while the other two discuss with each other. They do not hear what the teacher is saying, and they may end up permitting something forbidden in עריות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we may not teach סתרי עריות to three. It answers that this is simple logic about how a class of three behaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא searched for a פסוק as the source, and every attempt was pushed off. Now, following רב אשי's explanation, the source is plain reasoning. Two students both stay focused on the teacher, but a third creates a side conversation, and that side conversation can lead to a wrong, lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Logical reasoning, as opposed to a source from a פסוק
Discusses back and forth (literally 'takes and gives')
Bends his ear, meaning he listens closely
To permit something that is really forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not that three students are less smart. The worry is that a group of three tends to split into a side conversation, so two of them miss the teacher's explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the long search for a פסוק. The limit of 'not before three' rests on practical reasoning about how students learn.

phrases.english: What is the reason? It is logical reasoning.
phrases.notes: He is asking why סתרי עריות can't be taught to three, the way רב אשי just explained the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּי תְרֵי כִּי יָתְבִי קַמֵּי רַבַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: When two students sit before their teacher,
one discusses back and forth with his teacher,
and the other bends his ear to the learning.

phrases.aramaic: תְּלָתָא, חַד שָׁקֵיל וְטָרֵי בַּהֲדֵי רַבֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: With three, one discusses with his teacher,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנָךְ תְּרֵי שָׁקְלוּ וְטָרוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: and those other two discuss with each other,
and they do not know what their teacher is saying,
and they may come to permit something forbidden in forbidden relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רב אשי's reading of the משנה from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why may סתרי עריות not be taught before three?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Logic: with three students, two may talk among themselves, miss the teacher's words, and wrongly permit something forbidden.

steps.title: Then the whole Torah should have this limit too
steps.stepSummary: If the worry is that students miss the teacher's words and rule wrongly, that worry applies to every topic in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the whole Torah should also be taught to no more than two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason just given. The same worry seems to apply to every area of Torah, not only עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason in step 19 has nothing in it that is special to עריות. Two students in any subject could miss the teacher and permit something forbidden. So why is the rule limited to עריות?

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a phrase that opens a challenge
The entire Torah
Also

phrases.english: If so, the whole Torah too!
phrases.notes: He means the whole Torah should only be taught to two students at a time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 19 as too broad.
steps.kashyaTarget: The logical reason given in step 19
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worry about missing the teacher's words and permitting something forbidden applies to every Torah topic, so the limit should apply everywhere.

steps.title: עריות are different because people strongly desire them
steps.stepSummary: עריות are different because a person craves them, so there is a real danger he will rule leniently for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: עריות are different. As the Master said: a person's soul craves robbery and forbidden relations and desires them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עריות are special, because people have a strong desire for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In other topics, a student who missed the teacher's words has no personal push toward a lenient answer. With עריות, desire pulls him toward permitting, so the danger of a wrong ruling is much greater. That is why only עריות need the extra protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different
Robbery
Craves them and desires them

phrases.english: Forbidden relations are different,
for the Master said: robbery and forbidden relations —
a person's soul craves them and desires them.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets, 'of a person', and some don't. The meaning stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 by showing what is unique about עריות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: עריות carry a special risk that other topics do not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry about missing the teacher applies equally to all of Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only עריות, which a person strongly desires, carry a real risk of a self-serving lenient ruling.

steps.title: Then גזל should have this limit too
steps.stepSummary: The same teaching said people also crave גזל, so גזל should also be taught to no more than two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, robbery should also not be taught to three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The quoted teaching put גזל right next to עריות, so גזל should have the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 21 depended on desire. The very source it quoted says people desire גזל too. So the limit should apply to the laws of גזל as well.

phrases.english: If so, robbery too?
phrases.notes: He means: shouldn't the laws of robbery also be taught to no more than two students?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source quoted in step 21 to challenge its own conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 21 that desire makes עריות special
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same source lists גזל alongside עריות as something people crave, so גזל should share the restriction.

steps.title: The desire for עריות is stronger than the desire for גזל
steps.stepSummary: The desire for עריות is strong whether or not the object is present. The desire for גזל is strong only when the object is right in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: With עריות, whether the woman is in front of him or not, his evil inclination is strong. With robbery, when the object is in front of him his inclination is strong, but when it is not in front of him his inclination is not strong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing that the two desires are not equal. The desire for עריות is always active, but the desire for גזל needs the object to be right there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student learning the laws of גזל in the בית מדרש is not looking at someone else's property, so his desire is not stirred up. Thoughts of עריות can stir desire even with no one present, so studying them carries a real risk. That is why only עריות are limited to two students.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of him, present
Not in front of him, absent
His evil inclination is strong

steps.whatToRemember: The limit of 'not before three' applies only to סתרי עריות. It is based on logic: with three students, two may miss the teacher's words. The desire for עריות, unlike the desire for גזל, is strong even when the object is not present, so it could lead them to permit something forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the explanation of why the rule is special to עריות and does not apply to the rest of Torah or even to גזל.

phrases.aramaic: עֲרָיוֹת, בֵּין בְּפָנָיו בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו
phrases.english: With forbidden relations, whether in front of him or not in front of him,
his inclination is strong.
With robbery, in front of him, his inclination is strong;
not in front of him, his inclination is not strong.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲרָיוֹת, בֵּין בְּפָנָיו בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו נְפִישׁ יִצְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22 by separating the desire for עריות from the desire for גזל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction in the strength and nature of the desire
steps.terutzHavaAmina: גזל and עריות are equally desired, so both should be restricted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the desire for עריות is strong even when the object is absent, so only עריות are restricted to two students.

steps.title: Where does the rule about teaching creation to two come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that מעשה בראשית is not taught before two and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Nor מעשה בראשית before two.' From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving on to the next rule in the משנה and asking for its source. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For סתרי עריות the משנה limited the class to two students, and the source was logic. Here the limit is stricter: not even two, only one. So the גמרא wants to know where this stricter rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The secrets of how the world was created
Before two (students)
From where are these words learned? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: "Nor the act of Creation before two."
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of עריות and starts a new section on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for limiting the teaching of מעשה בראשית to a single student.

steps.title: The singular word 'ask' teaches one student only
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the singular 'שאל' in the פסוק that only one person may ask about creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'For ask now of the days past.' One person asks, but two do not ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The פסוק says 'ask' in the singular, so only one student at a time may ask about creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is in the grammar. The פסוק says 'ask' to one person, not 'ask' to a group. So the source here is a פסוק, unlike the עריות rule, which came from logic.

keyTerms.meaning: The early days, meaning the days of creation
One person asks

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for why מעשה בראשית is taught only one-on-one.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"For ask now of the days past"
phrases.notes: דברים 4:32. The word 'ask' here is said to one person, and that is the whole proof.

phrases.english: an individual may ask,
but two may not ask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular 'שאל' in דברים 4:32 teaches that only one student may ask about creation.

steps.title: No asking about before the world was created
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the פסוק limits the questions to the time from creation onward, not before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person may ask about what came before the world was created. So the פסוק says: 'Since the day that God created man upon the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and sets a limit on what you may ask. You may not ask about the time before the world existed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses a 'you might think' pattern: it suggests a possible idea and then rejects it with words from the פסוק. The words 'since the day God created' mark a starting point. Anything before that point is off-limits.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces an idea the ברייתא will reject)
Therefore the פסוק teaches (introduces the proof)
Before the world was created

phrases.english: One might have thought that a person may ask
about what came before the world was created,
therefore the verse states:

phrases.aramaic: ״לְמִן הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם עַל הָאָרֶץ״.
phrases.english: "Since the day that God created man upon the earth."
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק, דברים 4:32.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה/תשובה (the יכול and תלמוד לומר pattern inside the ברייתא)
steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִשְׁאַל אָדָם קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and sets the first limit on the subject matter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not ask about what came before the creation of the world.

steps.title: You may ask about the six days of creation
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא clarifies that the six days before man was created may still be asked about.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person may not ask about the six days of creation. So the פסוק says: 'of the days past, which were before you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא prevents us from limiting too much. Since the last step mentioned the creation of man, we might think the six days before man are off-limits, but they are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said 'since the day God created man.' Man was made on the sixth day, so that might seem to forbid asking about the earlier days. The words 'days past, which were before you' show that the days of creation before man are included.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not ask
The six days of creation
Which were before you

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two limits. Before the world existed is off-limits. The six days of creation, even before man was created, are allowed.

phrases.english: One might have thought that a person may not ask
about the six days of Creation,
therefore the verse states:
"Of the days past, which were before you."

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה/תשובה (the יכול and תלמוד לומר pattern inside the ברייתא)
steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִשְׁאַל אָדָם מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps the limit from step 26 from being read too broadly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may ask about the six days of creation, including the days before man was created.

steps.title: Ask only about what lies inside the world
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits questions to what lies within the ends of the heavens, and forbids asking what is above, below, before, or after.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person may ask what is above and what is below, what is before and what is after. So the פסוק says: 'From one end of the heavens to the other.' About what is from one end of the heavens to the other, you may ask. You may not ask what is above, what is below, what is before, or what is after.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets its last limit. You may ask about everything inside the world, but not about what lies beyond its edges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from one end of the heavens to the other' draw a boundary around the world. Questions inside that boundary are allowed. Questions about what is above it, below it, before it, or after it are not.

keyTerms.meaning: Above and below
Before and after
The end of the heavens, the edge of the world
You may ask

steps.whatToRemember: מעשה בראשית is taught to one student only, learned from the singular 'שאל.' The same פסוק sets the limits: nothing before the world was created, yes to the six days of creation, and only what lies inside the world, not what is above, below, before, or after it.

phrases.english: One might have thought that a person may ask
what is above and what is below,
what was before and what is after,
therefore the verse states:
"From one end of the heavens to the other."
phrases.notes: דברים 4:32

phrases.english: About what is from one end of the heavens to the other,
you may ask,
but you may not ask
what is above, what is below,
what was before, or what is after.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מסקנא (it closes the ברייתא's list of limits)
steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִשְׁאַל אָדָם מָה לְמַעְלָה וּמָה לְמַטָּה מָה לְפָנִים וּמָה לְאָחוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final limit of the ברייתא, this time about place instead of time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may ask about what lies inside the world, but not about what is above, below, before, or after it.
